text:
Trump is a big fan of a little snooze (file image)(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

We've all experienced it - as the day winds down, you're stuck in a meeting that should have been an email, and the urge builds to simply catch a brief nap and recharge. While most people manage to fight this impulse and push through, for President Trump the temptation appears frequently too powerful to overcome.

The Commander in Chief has been repeatedly observed apparently dozing off in public, including during crucial White House meetings, somber military ceremonies, and even while meeting the Queen.

Detractors have condemned Trump for literally falling asleep at the wheel, while others have expressed worry about the President, who turns 80 on Sunday, June 14. Here are six times the President has been caught apparently falling asleep in public.

Just this week the President was caught apparently enjoying a brief power nap during a press conference in the Oval Office. In footage shared on X, formerly Twitter, Trump can be seen sitting at his desk with his eyes shut, tilting slightly to his right, before appearing to stir and open his eyes, reports the Mirror US.

The footage was captured during a press conference announcing the removal of restrictions on commercial fishing in certain protected areas of the Pacific. Trump can be seen napping while Alaska governor Mike Dunleavy speaks on the significance of fishing to America's economy.

This wasn't even the first such incident this week. On Monday, the President attended Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden, watching the New York Knicks take on the San Antonio Spurs.

Despite presenting himself as a longtime Knicks supporter, a widely circulated clip shows Trump, seated alongside team owner James Dolan and his granddaughter Kai Trump, closing his eyes and folding his hands in his lap. His head appears to droop for approximately 45 seconds — a telltale sign he had dozed off — before he seemingly jolts awake.

Dolan, however, later denied that the President had fallen asleep. Appearing on WFAN's The Carton Show, he stated: "Where do they get this? I was with him the whole time. We were talking the whole time. Unless he was sleepwalking he was very much awake, he was very much engaged."

Just weeks prior, Trump was observed nodding off at a solemn Memorial Day ceremony at Arlington Cemetery. Video clips circulating across social media appeared to show Trump asleep during the May event.

After reviewing the footage, one physician suggested the President may be experiencing a specific medical condition. Speaking to CNN, Dr. Jonathan Reiner stated: "The president has severe daytime somnolence. He falls asleep very often.

"He's fallen asleep in the Oval Office on multiple occasions with people talking to him in the cabinet room, and I was concerned yesterday that he might have fallen asleep at Arlington National Cemetery during Memorial Day observances. Chronic insomnia is a severe illness. It can result in an increase in risk of dementia, decrease in cognitive effects in older people."

A turbulent White House Cabinet meeting in December 2025 saw the President appear to nod off while Secretary of State Marco Rubio showered him with compliments. Video from the two-hour session shows Trump's eyes starting to droop and shut as Rubio recounted his supposed recent achievements.

"I think you deserve tremendous credit for the transformational aspect of our foreign policy," Rubio said. "For the first time in probably four decades, the American foreign policy is driven by what is good for America and Americans. Whether it makes us safer and stronger and more prosperous. If it is, he's for it. If it doesn't, he's against it. And that sort of clarity is transformational."

In January, Trump told The Wall Street Journal that he doesn't fall asleep in public, but merely closes his eyes periodically. "It's very relaxing to me," he said. "Sometimes they'll take a picture of me blinking, blinking, and they'll catch me with the blink."

If there's one setting where maximum alertness is essential, it's inside a courtroom. Yet that apparently failed to hold Trump's attention, as he reportedly dozed off repeatedly while facing charges related to allegedly distributing up to $130,000 in 'hush money' to adult film actress Stormy Daniels in a bid to prevent her from discussing a purported affair.

Journalists present in the Manhattan courtroom during April 2024 documented observing the then-former President drifting off during the proceedings. On the New York Times live blog, Maggie Haberman noted: "Trump appears to be sleeping. His head keeps dropping down and his mouth goes slack."

Trump - who was then campaigning for a second White House term following his 2020 defeat to Joe Biden - was convicted on all 34 counts of falsifying business records, though he received an unconditional discharge as his sentence. He is currently appealing the conviction.

For most people, a Buckingham Palace visit would provide sufficient excitement to maintain wakefulness. Apparently not for Trump, however. During his initial presidential term, he received an invitation for a UK state visit, meeting Queen Elizabeth II and attending a state dinner held in his honor.

Observers were perplexed when he seemed to doze off during the Queen's welcoming remarks. The Monarch was discussing the strong ties between the UK and USA when Trump was observed closing his eyes multiple times - at one moment even jerking suddenly, as though startling himself awake.

Online commenters lashed out at the President, with one user stating: "You fell asleep during THE QUEEN'S speech! You are a total embarrassment to our country and the world."
